title: Try the finger test
body: Push a finger 2–3 cm into the soil before watering. Dry? Water deeply. Damp? Wait a day.

title: Water early
body: Early morning is the best time to water. Less is lost to heat, and leaves dry before night.

title: Pinch your basil
body: Pinch the tips of basil and mint often. Each pinch makes the plant grow bushier.

title: Give pots a quarter turn
body: Rotate each pot a quarter turn every week so all sides get light and growth stays even.

title: Check under the leaves
body: Pests hide on the underside of leaves. Take 2 minutes today to look at a few plants.

title: Drainage holes matter
body: A pot without drainage holes holds water at the roots. Always choose pots with holes.

title: Wipe dusty leaves
body: A damp cloth removes dust so leaves can absorb more light. Do it once a month.

title: Remove dead leaves
body: Pick off yellow or dead leaves and spent flowers. The plant then spends energy on new growth.

title: Mulch beats the heat
body: A layer of dry leaves or straw on the soil keeps roots cool and cuts evaporation.

title: Start small
body: Two or three healthy plants teach you more than a crowded balcony. Add more when you feel ready.

title: Match plant to light
body: Tomato and marigold love full sun. Snake plant and pothos are happy in low light.

title: Feed lightly
body: Fertilise only actively growing plants and follow the label. When unsure, use half the dose.

title: Use fresh potting mix
body: Mix garden soil, compost and coco peat, with a little sand for drainage. Fresh mix helps roots breathe.

title: Keep a garden diary
body: Write down what you water, what you plant, and what changes. Small notes make you a better gardener.

title: Compost your kitchen waste
body: Vegetable peels and tea leaves make rich compost. Add dry leaves too, and avoid oil and meat.

title: Spot the signs of stress
body: Yellow leaves often mean overwatering. Brown crispy tips often mean dry air or too little water.

title: Neem oil in the evening
body: Spray diluted neem oil in the evening, not in strong sun. Test on one leaf first.

title: Repot only one size up
body: Move to a pot just 2–4 cm wider. A pot that is too big keeps soil wet for too long.

title: Group pots together
body: Plants placed together share humidity and stay cooler. Great for hot North Indian summers.

title: Deadhead to keep blooms
body: Pinch off faded marigolds and petunias. The plant will make more flowers.

title: Harvest little and often
body: Cut herbs just above a pair of leaves with clean scissors. Regular harvesting keeps them growing.

title: Protect from afternoon heat
body: In peak summer, move delicate pots out of direct afternoon sun and water in the morning.

title: Propagate a cutting
body: Cut a 10–15 cm money plant stem below a node and place it in water. Roots appear in 2–4 weeks.

title: Empty the saucers
body: Water left standing in a saucer can rot roots. Empty it 15 minutes after watering.

title: Use room-temperature water
body: Very cold water shocks roots. Let your watering can sit out for a while first.

title: Layer your balcony
body: Tall plants at the back, medium in the middle, low at the front. Layers make small spaces look lush.

title: Reuse water
body: Water from washing vegetables is perfect for ornamental plants. Small habits save a lot of water.

title: Be patient
body: Plants grow slowly. Change one thing at a time and give it a week or two before judging.

title: Plan the next season
body: Check the seasonal guide and decide what to sow next. Good gardeners plan ahead.

title: Enjoy the process
body: Spend five quiet minutes with your plants today. Gardening is good for you as well as for them.
